chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Do the act of kindness to the one who is deserving of it, and to the one who is not deserving of it; for if he is not deserving of it, then you become the one who is deserving of it.

key_terms.أَهْلِهِ: Deserving/worthy (referring to the recipient or giver)

ai.seo_question: How should one treat those who do not deserve kindness according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) expands the concept of al-ma'ruf by distinguishing between reciprocal kindness to the deserving and gratuitous kindness to the undeserving. This teaching highlights the Shia emphasis on ihsan (excellence in conduct), where the giver actively confers 'deservingness' upon the recipient through their generosity, thereby transforming the social dynamic and securing greater spiritual merit.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Do the act of kindness to the one who is deserving of it, rather than to the one who is not deserving of it, for if he does not happen to be deserving of it, so you would become the one who is deserving of it’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj who has said the following:“Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

you should provide Benevolent Assistance to those who deserve and to those who (in reality) are un-deserving; if the recipient does not deserve it, you are considered a provider of Benevolent Assistance.”
